column4: rx_matchfn is the shared function type ptrdiff_t rx_matchfn(const rx_ctx *ctx), defined in §2.
Every artifact declares ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match(const rx_ctx *ctx).
<prefix>_match matches at exactly ctx->pos: a match starting anywhere else is not reported.
The anchoring promise of <prefix>_match is the semantic a caller can rely on; it is deliberately not a claim about how the artifact is built.
On a VM artifact the <prefix>_match emitter has no search loop.
A DFA artifact's <prefix>_match takes one of two forms, named in <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH and rx_info.match_form (§6.3).
Measured: the DFA forms of <prefix>_match give the same answers; only the anchoring promise is contractual.
Form "unwrapped": the artifact carries a THIRD machine, the tables of its forward scan WITHOUT the start-anywhere self-loop, run forward from ctx->pos.
Under "unwrapped" there is no later start to reject and no backwards pass to recover a start with.
Under "unwrapped" a failing <prefix>_match probe stops at the first byte that cannot continue a match beginning at ctx->pos.
Under "unwrapped" a succeeding <prefix>_match costs one forward scan rather than a forward and a reverse scan.
The "unwrapped" form reports the same length the "search-filter" form reports, on every input (argued in anchored_match_unwrapped.md §3).
Form "search-filter": <prefix>_match runs the artifact's ordinary UNANCHORED search and rejects any match whose start is not ctx->pos.
search-filter is still the <prefix>_match form on some artifacts.
On a failing <prefix>_match under "search-filter" the underlying search does not know the question is anchored and may skim the rest of the subject for a later match the filter discards.
The state-0 memchr skip keeps that failing-probe cost a skim rather than a per-byte walk, where an anchored body fails at the first divergent byte.
A caller issuing many expected-to-fail <prefix>_match probes against long subjects is in the "search-filter" form's worst case, and can read off the artifact whether it is in that form.
Exactly five populations take the "search-filter" form for <prefix>_match.
Population 1 of "search-filter": an artifact whose engine is the per-start attempt loop (<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "attempt", i.e. a ^- or \G-bearing pattern).
Population 2 of "search-filter": an artifact that matches nothing (<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "empty").
Population 3 of "search-filter": an artifact whose anchored machine exceeded a DFA cap; this is a SELECTION OUTCOME, never a refusal.
Population 4 of "search-filter": any build under -fno-anchored-dfa (tuning.md §2.15).
Population 5 of "search-filter": an artifact whose anchored machine pcrec DROPPED so the artifact fits under an emitted-size cap (limits.md §8 "The optional-contributor drop"), since [K53-SELRETRY].
The size-cap-drop population is the only one where a caller could have had the faster form and lost it to a size limit rather than to the pattern's shape.
The size-cap-drop population is identifiable by <PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry".
Raising --max-emit-bytes gets the anchored machine back for a size-cap-retry artifact.
<prefix>_match returns the matched length (>= 0) on a match at ctx->pos.
<prefix>_match returns 0 for a zero-length match at ctx->pos.
<prefix>_match returns -1 on no match.
<prefix>_match may return a typed give-up code (§4).
<prefix>_match may return one of §3.1's caller refusals at ctx->pos: PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS (K50).
Under -futf-check <prefix>_match returns PCREC_ERR_UTF from the same check at the same position as <prefix>_search, in the same order (guard first) and over the same checked range.
Under -fstartpos-guard=align a misaligned ctx->pos makes <prefix>_match answer -1 (no match begins inside a character), after the check has run from the aligned position.
<prefix>_match delivers no captures: ctx->caps is an input (§5), not an output channel.
<prefix>_match has no parameter to write group offsets into.
A top-level caller of <prefix>_match passes ctx->ncap = 0 and ctx->caps = NULL (self-contained per rx_matchfn's contract).
Every artifact declares ptrdiff_t <prefix>_match_caps(const rx_ctx *ctx, ptrdiff_t (*caps_out)[2]).
<prefix>_match_caps has the same anchoring promise as <prefix>_match (match at exactly ctx->pos) and the same two forms (§3.2).
Under "unwrapped" <prefix>_match_caps delegates to <prefix>_match and fills the spans itself.
Under "unwrapped" caps_out[0] is [ctx->pos, ctx->pos + length) by construction rather than by a filter that proved it.
On success <prefix>_match_caps writes all of caps_out[0..<PREFIX>_NCAPS-1] (same completed-match discipline as <prefix>_search).
On success of <prefix>_match_caps, caps_out[0] is [ctx->pos, ctx->pos + length).
On a captures-on build caps_out[k] is capturing group k for k >= 1, in the pattern's own left-to-right numbering.
rx_group_entry.slot exists for a future in which a build delivers a different slot for a group; on today's builds no such indirection is in play and slot == group number.
D61: for the PRIMARY pattern's own groups on a captures-on build, slot == number is PERMANENT.
The different-slot latitude applies only to future ref-bearing rows (§6), whose delivered slots APPEND after the primary prefix and never displace slots 1..ngroups.
On failure <prefix>_match_caps leaves caps_out untouched, and a give-up counts as a failure for this rule.
Every negative return of <prefix>_match_caps leaves the caller's caps_out array exactly as it was.
The generated source states outright: "caps_out is UNTOUCHED on every negative return, give-up included".
The same untouched-on-negative-return rule holds for <prefix>_search's caps.
<prefix>_match_caps reads ctx->caps/ctx->ncap as ordinary rx_ctx input, unrelated to caps_out.
A top-level <prefix>_match_caps call passes ncap=0, caps=NULL exactly like <prefix>_match.
Entry choice: no start position known and/or no captures wanted -> <prefix>_search.
Entry choice: start position known, captures wanted, no search loop wanted -> <prefix>_match_caps.
Entry choice: neither offsets nor a loop wanted -> <prefix>_match.
The discriminator between the entries is whether the start position is KNOWN, never whether captures are wanted.
<prefix>_search delivers full captures when handed a caps buffer (§3.1), so first match plus its groups is one <prefix>_search call.
<prefix>_match_caps is only for the anchored case.
The three entries are not interchangeable views of one answer on the give-up axis.
§4's uniformity is about the CODE SPACE (which values mean what), not about which entry gives up on a given input.
Whether a budget is exhausted is a property of the entry point, because the entries do different amounts of work; it goes both ways.
Measured: (a|aa)+b built --step-budget=3 over "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaX": <prefix>_search returns 0 (its DFA prefilter resolves the question without entering the VM).
Measured: (a|aa)+b built --step-budget=3 over "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaX": <prefix>_match and <prefix>_match_caps both return -2.
Measured: (a|aa)+b-family artifact built --backtrack-frames=1 over "xxaaaaab": <prefix>_search returns -3.
Measured: on that --backtrack-frames=1 artifact over "xxaaaaab" both anchored entries return a clean -1, because anchoring at position 0 fails immediately and spends no frame.
A caller must handle give-ups on whichever entry it actually calls.
A caller must not infer from one entry's clean answer that another entry would give one.
Every artifact declares extern const struct rx_info <prefix>_info.
<prefix>_info is one instance per artifact, a link-time constant, with no runtime cost to build.
<prefix>_info is not strictly .rodata: struct rx_info holds pointers (pattern, engine_why, and others), so the object needs load-time relocation.
CHECK: Measured with readelf on a default build of 'a(b|c)+d' (struct since grown, size is historical): rx_info is a 104-byte object in section .data.rel.ro.local, not .rodata.
CHECK: Measured on that build: .data.rel.ro.local carries exactly two R_X86_64_64 relocations, one per embedded string pointer (pattern, engine_why); struct has since gained more pointer fields.
The strings rx_info points at are in .rodata.
<prefix>_info has no run-time initializer and no constructor; its cost is relocations at load, not zero.
The give-up-collapse-to--1 rule of match_api_m4.md §3 as originally written does not exist in the shipped artifact, on either engine; D49 supersedes D42.3.
A DFA artifact's <prefix>_match is a wrapper that calls <prefix>_search(ctx->subject, ctx->len, ctx->pos, caps) with a local caps[NCAPS][2] and returns found if found < 0.
In a DFA artifact's <prefix>_match, give-up codes PROPAGATE rather than collapsing to -1 (D49).
In a DFA artifact the give-up propagation branch is unreachable (no counter to exhaust) but written uniformly on purpose, because rx_matchfn has one contract and a later engine may share the emitter.
The DFA artifact's <prefix>_match local caps array is zero-initialized (= {{0}}), because of gcc -O1 false maybe-uninitialized (K28).
A DFA artifact's <prefix>_match returns the <prefix>_search result unchanged (cast to ptrdiff_t) when it is negative.
A DFA artifact's <prefix>_match returns -1 if <prefix>_search found != 1 or caps[0][0] != ctx->pos.
A DFA artifact's <prefix>_match otherwise returns caps[0][1] - caps[0][0].
A VM artifact's <prefix>_match returns -1 if ctx->pos > ctx->len.
A VM artifact's <prefix>_match initializes a work struct (<prefix>_work_init) and calls <prefix>_match_impl(ctx, &w, ctx->len).
A VM artifact's <prefix>_match returns the impl's result with no translation and no clamp.
The VM impl's return space is >= 0, -1, or one of the three R_ sentinels, which are the ERR_ codes.
The DFA body's unreachable propagation is evidence that the emitter WRITES the propagation, not that it ever happens; the VM is the live evidence.
Measured: (a|aa)+b built --step-budget=3 returns -2 from <prefix>_match and <prefix>_match_caps.
Measured: (a|aa)+b built --backtrack-frames=1 returns -3 from all three entries, <prefix>_search included, on subject "ab".
The DFA body's found != 1 || caps[0][0] != ctx->pos test is the only thing making that engine honor §3.2's anchoring promise.
The caps initializer in the DFA <prefix>_match is never observed and changes no answer.

A single-dead-state DFA makes rx_search always return 0; gcc -O1 inlines it and reports the caps array maybe-uninitialized though the read is unreachable; the initializer prevents a -Werror consumer build failure (K28).
The same caps declaration and initializer appear in <prefix>_match_caps and in the standalone main().
Measured: restructuring the found != 1 test instead of initializing caps does NOT silence the maybe-uninitialized report.
D49 supersedes D42.3 and rules the uniform-codes contract the artifacts implement.
A caller that only tests r < 0 for did-it-match is unaffected by give-up codes being distinct.
A caller doing an exact == -1 comparison sees give-up codes as distinct values, not folded into -1.
CHECK: An artifact generated before 2026-08-18 carries an emitted rx_matchfn ABI comment saying values < -1 are reserved and none is produced; that comment is false for such artifacts.
Where an old artifact's comment and the spec disagree, the spec is the contract; the artifact's behavior always matched the spec, not its own comment.
The emitted rx_matchfn comment now states the give-up space (§2 quotes it verbatim), and lib/pcrec.h's generated-searcher comment names the negative return space too.
There is no native end-anchored entry: no search-style call meaning match and require the match to reach the subject's end.
§3.1-§3.3's three entries answer does a match exist starting here, never does a match exist covering here to n.
A caller wanting PCRE2_ANCHORED|PCRE2_ENDANCHORED semantics compiles (?:P)\z (P in a non-capturing group followed by \z) and calls any of §3.1-§3.3.
Use \z, not $: $ admits a trailing newline at default options ((?m) off), which is not the subject's end.
Measured: (?:foo)$ compiled --no-captures matches "foo\n" at [0,3), while (?:foo)\z on the identical subject reports no match.
\z is module assertions' unconditional end-of-subject assertion and admits nothing after it.
Of $, \Z, \z only \z admits nothing after the subject end at default options.
Running the anchored entry and testing length == n is SUFFICIENT for end-anchored matching but not NECESSARY.
Leftmost-first preference picks the FIRST alternative that matches, never the one reaching farthest.
Measured: a|ab compiled --no-captures run anchored over "ab" reports [0,1).
Measured: (?:a|ab)\z over "ab" reports [0,2).
\z forces backtracking past the a branch's failure (position 1 is not the subject's end) into the ab branch, so the engine does the end-anchoring search.
The (?:P)\z idiom is a ruled-permanent idiom, not a stopgap awaiting a dedicated generation axis ([OS-4], D77 2026-08-25).
A whole-subject/end-anchored generation axis (single artifact answering both questions, or an emitted skip loop stopping one byte short for \z) is explicitly NOT being built now.
The idiom costs two artifacts (one ordinary compile, one (?:P)\z compile) and leaves a final-byte DFA skip gap, recorded as a general-optimization candidate ([OS-4]).
Any such \z optimization is not scoped to one caller: (?:P)\z benefits identically to every other \z-bearing pattern.

A \z-bearing pattern still selects the DFA, and its <prefix>_match runs the artifact's own anchored machine from ctx->pos rather than the unanchored search with a start filter (the "unwrapped" form), since 2026-08-29.
Measured on the (?:P)\z idiom over the comparative bench's 85 compliance subjects: the matching split goes from 2.074x behind the backtracking VM to 1.031x.
Measured on the same 85 subjects: short valid emails go from 1.223x behind the backtracking VM to 0.482x (ahead of it).
Nothing about the (?:P)\z idiom itself changed; the entry got cheaper.
Verified live: (?:foo|bar)\z (--no-captures) stamps RX_DFA_SCAN "unanchored".
Verified live: (?:foo|bar)\z (--no-captures) stamps RX_DFA_PREFILTER "byte-class-bounded".
The \z wrapper changes the emitted candidate-start filter, not just the trailing assertion; the idiom does not anchor the START, only the end.
byte-class-bounded is the bounded form for a $/\Z/\z view, where a skip may not pass the position whose accept has not yet been evaluated (§6.3).
Verified live: (?:foo)\z (single literal, no alternation) stamps the single-candidate form "memchr-bounded".
Neither idiom use produces RX_DFA_SCAN "attempt" by itself; that shape is what a LEADING ^ or \A selects (§6.3), an orthogonal axis.
§4 states the give-up CODES; the numeric trigger defaults (step and work budgets, frame/trail capacities) are limits.md's subject and are not restated in match_api.
limits.md also carries the compile-time state-count ceilings, the two-tier entry's numeric cost model, and the K33/K34 documented-divergence detail.
<prefix>_search, rx_matchfn (hence <prefix>_match and any callout) and <prefix>_match_caps all report engine give-up in the same code space: a negative return strictly below -1.
The same give-up value means the same thing at every entry.
The code-space uniformity says nothing about when a give-up happens; which entry gives up on a given input is a property of that entry.
The step and work budgets bound ONE attempt, and an un-suffixed entry may make TWO attempts.
§10.9's tiered entry re-runs the match on the stamped default after a PCREC_ERR_FRAMES give-up on its fast tier, with both budgets REFILLED.
Refilling both budgets on the deep attempt makes the tiered answer identical to a single-tier artifact's (stated in §10.9).
A single call to <prefix>_search/_match/_match_caps can spend up to TWICE the step budget and twice the work budget before returning.
A returned PCREC_ERR_STEPS still means the deep attempt exhausted a full budget.
The _in entries have no tier and are bounded by one budget.
A caller needing a hard bound on the work ONE call may do uses an _in entry or -fno-tiered-entry (tuning.md §2.12).
PCREC_ERR_STEPS is -2 (step budget exhausted give-up).
PCREC_ERR_FRAMES is -3 (frame capacity exhausted give-up).
PCREC_ERR_WORK is -4 (work budget exhausted give-up).
PCREC_ERR_RECURSE is -5, reserved with no producer yet (D71 item 1, [DD-14]).
PCREC_ERR_FLOOR is -5; give-ups are the range [FLOOR, -2], and values below FLOOR are reserved (D49).
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL is -6, below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up (D71 item 1, [DD-14]).
PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS is -7, below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up; a mid-character startpos was REFUSED ([K50]).
PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR is -8, below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up; an UNSET or ill-formed variable value was REFUSED ([VAR]).
PCREC_ERR_UTF is -9, below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR: NOT a give-up; an ill-formed subject was REFUSED (-futf-check) ([UTF-VALID]).
PCREC_ERR_STEPS/_FRAMES/_WORK/_FLOOR are unprefixed pcrec-CONTRACT constants in the shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H block (§2) (D60); the per-<PREFIX> spelling is DELETED, not aliased.
The PCREC_ERR_* block is byte-identical across prefixes: a -p foo build of the same pattern emits the same lines as -p rx (§1/§2 cross-prefix identity).

PCREC_ERR_RECURSE is reserved now; the recursion-depth counter that would produce it is NOT in the default artifact (D71 item 1; a future [V-H] diagnostic-generation axis, a separate emitted variant, not a runtime flag).
No arm in any emitter returns PCREC_ERR_RECURSE today; it is unreachable on every artifact.
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL is BELOW the floor and is NOT a give-up.
D49 reserves everything strictly below PCREC_ERR_FLOOR for a future abort semantic; PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL is that semantic's first producer.
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL means the artifact detected its OWN inconsistency (a compile-time width analysis pcrec_maxw disagreeing with what the emitter walked), never a runtime resource give-up.
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL's one producer today is module lookaround's negative-polarity lookbehind END-CHECK ((?<!X)).
On negative-polarity lookbehind a declined branch is the assertion succeeding, so a width disagreement would be a FALSE MATCH; the hard PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL return prevents it.
PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL has never been observed on a correctly analyzed pattern; the check is provably redundant for the width class lookaround ships and is emitted as a self-consistency guard.
A top-level entry (<prefix>_search, <prefix>_match, <prefix>_match_caps) PROPAGATES PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL to its caller exactly like a give-up and does not trap.
The trap on below-the-floor codes belongs at composed call sites, not at top-level entries.

Verified on a DFA-only artifact (--no-captures; no counter exists; give-up codes reserved-but-unreachable) and a captures-default VM artifact (RX_STEP_BUDGET/RX_WORK_BUDGET/RX_BT_FRAMES/RX_TRAIL_FRAMES present, counters live).
A DFA-compiled artifact never RETURNS PCREC_ERR_STEPS/FRAMES/WORK (no counter to exhaust).
The PCREC_ERR_* constants are defined in every artifact, DFA included.
Measured: a DFA artifact built --no-captures --emit-main emits the three-way handler text (if (rc == PCREC_ERR_STEPS), PCREC_ERR_FRAMES, PCREC_ERR_WORK).
Emitting the constants and handler text on a DFA artifact is deliberate: it lets a caller's switch written today survive a later compile of the same pattern selecting the VM.
Every generated call site that invokes an rx_matchfn (a callout, a composed submatcher) must enforce if (ret < PCREC_ERR_FLOOR) __builtin_trap();.
The below-the-floor trap binds call sites that call INTO another rx_matchfn, not an exported entry's own internal return.
No such composed/callout call sites are emitted by pcrec today (callout code generation has no producer yet).
Trapping on PCREC_ERR_INTERNAL at a composed call site is the design, not a gap.
PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS is the second below-the-floor code and a REFUSAL of the call rather than a report about the engine.
Every value in [PCREC_ERR_FLOOR, -2] says the engine ran and exhausted something.
PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS says the caller named a startpos (or ctx->pos) that is not a character boundary of the artifact's encoding; no attempt was made and no budget was touched.
Every artifact DEFINES PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS and only some can RETURN it.
Under the byte encoding every position is a character boundary, so no startpos guard is emitted and PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS is unreachable.
The PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS constant is emitted on byte-encoding artifacts anyway so a caller's switch survives a later compile under a different encoding.
A composed call site TRAPS on PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS, by the below-the-floor rule.
After K50 every position an ENGINE generates is a character boundary, so a composed callee handed a non-boundary means the engine broke its own rule.
PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS renumbers nothing: PCREC_ERR_FLOOR is unchanged at -5 and the give-up partition is unchanged.
PCREC_ERR_UTF (-9) is the third caller refusal and the first below-the-floor code a composed call site propagates.
PCREC_ERR_UTF means an artifact compiled with -futf-check found an ill-formed sequence beginning in the checked range [startpos - LB, n) (§3.1); the call was refused before any attempt.
On PCREC_ERR_UTF the caller's caps are untouched.
On PCREC_ERR_UTF, <prefix>_valid_upto(s, n, startpos) (§3.1.2) gives the offset of the ill-formedness.
PCREC_ERR_UTF is one code for every kind of ill-formedness; pcrec owes the refusal and the offset, not PCRE2's twenty PCRE2_ERROR_UTF8_* values (D26).
Every artifact DEFINES PCREC_ERR_UTF; only a -futf-check artifact under an encoding with ill-formed byte strings can RETURN it.
A composed call site PROPAGATES PCREC_ERR_UTF and does NOT trap (D133 Q11); this is the one exception to the below-the-floor trap rule.
-6 and -7 at a composed callee mean the ENGINE broke its own rule, but -9 is caused by the CALLER'S DATA: a checking callee's LB may reach before the outer call's range.
The composed-call-site trap is if (ret < PCREC_ERR_FLOOR && ret != PCREC_ERR_UTF) __builtin_trap(); and a -9 is returned outward unchanged.
No composed call sites are emitted today; the PCREC_ERR_UTF trap line is recorded so the first producer inherits it.
PCREC_ERR_UTF renumbers nothing: it is a new value in the region D49 reserved, below PCREC_ERR_UNSET_VAR (-8).
PCREC_ERR_FRAMES names a RESOURCE, not an array and not an owner.
Two distinct capacities can exhaust and both report PCREC_ERR_FRAMES: the resume stack (<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES) and its sibling undo trail (<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES).
Which capacity ran out is not reported; a caller must not assume it was the one whose macro is named frames.
Measured on ^(a(?1)?b)$: the artifact gives up with the trail full and TWO THIRDS of its resume stack still unused (frame_buffer_design.md §4).
PCREC_ERR_FRAMES, with the same meaning, also covers a caller-supplied buffer ([DD-14.FB], §10.3), and does not say whose buffer it was.
<prefix>_search's 1/0 contract is unchanged: the give-up reservation adds outcomes and does not renumber match/no-match.
<prefix>_search's return is not two-valued, so if (<prefix>_search(...)) reads a give-up as a match; a caller must test == 1 for matched (§3.1).
rx_ctx.caps is declared const ptrdiff_t (*caps)[2], half-open [start, end) pairs.
<PREFIX>_NCAPS is a per-artifact compile-time constant.
PCREC_UNSET is ((ptrdiff_t)-1), a pcrec-contract unprefixed constant (§2, D60).
PCREC_UNSET is emitted once in the shared PCREC_RX_ABI_H block (§2); the per-<PREFIX> spelling <PREFIX>_UNSET is DELETED, not aliased.
<PREFIX>_NCAPS stays per-prefix because its VALUE varies per artifact.
Unset capture representation is {-1, -1} in BOTH slots of a pair.
caps[k][0] < 0 is a sufficient unset test.
Index 0 of caps is always the whole match.
<PREFIX>_NCAPS >= 1 always.
<PREFIX>_NCAPS is a property of the compiled ARTIFACT, not of the pattern text.
A DFA-compiled artifact, capture-bearing pattern or not, always emits <PREFIX>_NCAPS 1.
<PREFIX>_NCAPS > 1 implies the VM engine was selected.
Verified: 'a(b|c)+d' compiled --no-captures emits RX_NCAPS 1 with rx_info.ngroups == 1 (the pattern has a group; the artifact delivers no slot for it).
Verified: 'a(b|c)+d' compiled with captures on (default since M4.5) emits RX_NCAPS 2.
rx_info.ncaps == <PREFIX>_NCAPS always (a structural invariant of the build).
Every pair 0..<PREFIX>_NCAPS-1 is written on a completed match; no watermark is needed at read time.
On a failed match the caller's caps array is left untouched, and an engine give-up is a failure for this rule.
Every negative return from an anchored entry, and a 0 or a give-up code from <prefix>_search, leaves the caps array exactly as the caller left it.
No attempt is made to write {-1,-1} into the caps array on failure; the return value alone communicates failure.
The caps array is caller-owned, fixed-size and compile-time-sized: a caller declares ptrdiff_t caps[<PREFIX>_NCAPS][2] on the stack.
Nothing in the generated contract allocates.
ctx->caps handed to a callout mid-match is valid for the duration of that one call only.
The engine rewrites the same ctx->caps storage after the callout call (trail-based undo); a callout retaining the pointer and reading it later is the embedder's bug, not a pcrec contract violation.
A completed match's caps are stable until the next match call reusing the same buffer.
The matcher may overwrite the caps buffer between separate calls, but never mid-splice.
Every capture slot 0..ncaps-1 is written on a completed match.
The two §5.1 capture-value rules were measured three-way unanimous (python re, libpcre2, pcrec agree) and are part of the shipped contract.
Cross-iteration retention: a group inside a quantifier that did not run in the FINAL iteration retains its value from the last iteration in which it did run.
((a)|(b))* matched against "ab" reports group 2 as [0,1), not unset.
Unset means never participated in the whole match, not did not participate in the match's last iteration.
An empty final iteration still overwrites: an empty iteration's write is a write.
(a*)* and (a?)* matched against "aaa" both report group 1 as [3,3).
A caller reading caps[k] after a successful match need not reason about which iteration produced the value; the slot holds the group's last-executed span or is genuinely unset.
A slot is unset only if the group never ran at all, in any iteration, anywhere in the match.

The §5.2 non-requirements are scoped to the MATCH path (generated matcher and its caps buffers); the library's compile path does allocate and has a lifecycle (§8 pcrec_output/pcrec_output_free) that must still be honored.
Non-requirement: no ovector sizing negotiation; the group count is a compile-time fact.
Non-requirement: no match-data object, no allocation, no lifecycle to manage on the match path.
Non-requirement: no run-time does-group-N-exist query; a compile-time check is the caller's own business.
Non-requirement: no run-time name lookup for template resolution; a future substitution compiler resolves ${name} at pcrec-compile time.
Non-requirement: no partial-match or streaming window state.
Non-requirement: no callout/callback context beyond what rx_ctx itself carries.
A callout binding's user data lives entirely in the rx_callout_ref the binding declares.
Nothing about which callout is firing is visible to rx_matchfn's own signature.
A generated matcher holds no mutable state of its own.
Every entry point's working state lives in its own stack frame and in the caller's caps buffer; tables, bitmaps and the rx_info instance are const.
Any number of threads may call the same artifact's entry points concurrently, provided each call has its own caps/caps_out buffer.
Sharing one caps buffer between concurrent calls is a data race in the CALLER's code; the matcher does not serialize it.
One thread may re-enter a matcher (e.g. from a callout), subject to the same distinct-buffer rule.
<prefix>_info is read-only and may be read from anywhere at any time.
Reentrancy/thread-safety is a CONTRACT binding on future emitters, not an observation about today's output.
An engine that wanted a mutable scratch buffer would have to change the spec first.
The thread-safety promise says nothing about how much STACK each concurrent call needs.
An artifact whose frame requirement is not statically bounded declares its whole run state as a local of the entry it was called through.
The tiered entry (§10.9) moves the stamped default storage off the entry's own frame onto a non-inlined internal function only a PCREC_ERR_FRAMES give-up reaches.
Measured on a -p rx --features all build of ^(a(?1)?b)$: <prefix>_search's stack frame is 3,184 bytes and the internal deep function's is 131,216 bytes.
Measured: a statically-bounded pattern pays nothing: a(b|c)+d's entry frame is 208 bytes.
A glibc-default 8 MB main thread is unaffected by the 131 KB frame class.
The fit criterion for a call is free STACK HEADROOM AT THE CALL SITE (entry + deep, 134,400 bytes for this artifact class), not thread-stack size as such.
A thread's nominal stack size equals the headroom available to a call only when the call happens at depth ~0 (limits.md §5).
Measured: at depth ~0 on a musl-default 128 KB thread, the ^(a(?1)?b)$ --features all artifact matches every subject the fast tier holds and faults only on one deep enough to escalate.
The remedy for small-stack callers is still the _in entries, and it is the only way to get a guarantee.
Which subjects escalate to the deep tier is a property of the pattern and the subject, not something a caller can bound in advance.
known_issues.md K33 carries the narrowed statement of the stack limitation.
tests/thread/run_stackdepth_tests.sh pins both halves: the small entry frame, and the deep tier still dying on a small stack.
The remedy SHIPS as §10's _in entries ([DD-14.FB], D71 item 2).
Measured: the _in entries' own frame is 144 bytes at -O2, 312 including the two statics they call through, and 224 at -O3 where gcc inlines the statics into both entries.
The 131 KB of default storage never reaches the _in entry's frame.
A caller on a small thread stack supplies its own storage via _in, so the arrays are not on that stack at all.
A caller who cannot use _in must size the thread for the artifact or compile with a smaller --backtrack-frames.
The default (un-suffixed) path is unchanged and still does not fit a small thread stack, deliberately: D73 keeps the stamped 2048/3072 capacities.
A caller who calls the un-suffixed entry of this artifact class from a small-stack thread has a live limitation (K33).
tests/thread/run_stackdepth_tests.sh reproduces on every run: the default entry dying on a 128 KB thread, and _search_in matching the same subject on the same thread.
Thread safety is GUARDED by shipped checks in make test (TS-1, TS-2) plus TS-3 for the library.
TS-1 (D19) is static: it scans every emitted file across nine emission shapes and fails on any non-const static object or any reference to a non-reentrant or allocating libc symbol.
TS-2 is dynamic under ThreadSanitizer: eight threads share ONE compiled matcher and search DIFFERENT subjects concurrently, across five patterns hitting five differently shaped emitted engines.
TS-2 requires every threaded result to equal a single-threaded baseline recorded before any thread was spawned.
TS-2's sabotage arm: a planted race in a scratch copy of the driver must be caught, or the check fails itself.
TS-3 runs eight threads each compiling its own pattern through pcrec_compile() concurrently, byte-matching a single-threaded baseline, TSan-instrumented and sabotage-validated.
pcrec_compile() is safe to call concurrently (§8 assumes it; TS-3 is the evidence).
struct rx_info is the reflection structure of an artifact.
rx_info.abi is an unsigned layout version, bump-on-change.
rx_info.flags is a uint64_t of PCREC_* option bits exactly as compiled.
rx_info.encoding is an int holding a PCREC_ENC_* value.
rx_info.ncaps is an int equal to <PREFIX>_NCAPS: this artifact's caps[] slot count, all-in.
rx_info.ngroups is an int counting capturing groups in the PATTERN TEXT: a lexical fact, independent of --no-captures and of engine selection.
On a COMPOSED artifact rx_info.ngroups is the TARGET pattern's own count; a bound definition's groups sit above it (D61, [DD-13b.W1.3]).
rx_info.nnames is an int: the number of rows in groups[] the PRIMARY pattern declared, always a PREFIX of the array.
rx_info.nnames is 0 when the pattern text declares no named group.
rx_info.nnames is 0 when module 'named-groups' is not ENABLED for this compile; this is a different reason from the pattern declaring none.
rx_info.nentries is the whole groups[] array's length; nnames counts only the primary pattern's rows.
rx_info.engine is an unsigned: PCREC_ENGINE_DFA = 1, PCREC_ENGINE_VM = 2.
rx_info.step_budget is an int64_t; -1 means none.
rx_info.work_budget is an int64_t; -1 means none.
rx_info.work_budget is the THIRD bound (D47 second addendum): forward work the fail label never sees, counted separately from step_budget.
rx_info.frame_capacity is an int64_t; -1 means unbounded.
rx_info.frame_capacity's -1 sentinel is NOT the sentinel the same-named pcrec_options field uses (asymmetry note).
rx_info.subject_ceiling is an int64_t; 0 means unset/not applicable.
A nonzero rx_info.subject_ceiling is the stamped honest ceiling for a residually-unbounded capture body.
rx_info.resume_frames is an int64_t: the stamped DEFAULT resume capacity in frames ([DD-14.FB]).
rx_info.resume_frames is 0 when the artifact has no resume stack (every DFA artifact).
rx_info.trail_frames is an int64_t: the stamped default trail capacity in trail entries.
rx_info.resume_frame_size is an int32_t: bytes per resume frame for THIS artifact.
rx_info.resume_frame_size is 0 on a DFA artifact.
rx_info.trail_frame_size is an int32_t: bytes per trail entry.
rx_info.pattern is a const char * holding the source pattern text as given to pcrec_compile().
rx_info.pattern_len is a size_t companion length of rx_info.pattern (§7).
rx_info.groups is a const rx_group_entry * that is NULL until the pattern text declares at least one named group.
When non-NULL, rx_info.groups is sorted by NAME (strcmp).
rx_info.engine_why is a const char * naming the forcing construct/reason, or NULL.
rx_info.engine_why also carries a prefilter note on hybrid-eligible artifacts.
rx_info.scan is a const char * ([DD-13c]): the DFA scan the artifact CONTAINS, "unanchored" / "attempt" / "empty", mirroring <PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN.
rx_info.scan is NULL when the artifact contains no DFA scan.
rx_info.prefilter is a const char * ([DD-13c]): the artifact's candidate-start mechanism, in whichever engine's vocabulary applies.
rx_info.prefilter is never NULL.
rx_info.match_form is a const char * ([ENG-ABS]): HOW <prefix>_match answers, "unwrapped" / "search-filter", mirroring <PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH.
rx_info.match_form is NULL on every artifact whose _match the DFA emitter did not write: every VM artifact, HYBRIDS INCLUDED (§6.3).
rx_info.name is a const char * ([DD-13b.W1.2]): this artifact's own name.
rx_info.name is NEVER NULL; a build that names nothing stamps its own <prefix>.
rx_info.nentries is an int ([DD-13b.W1.2]): the number of rows in groups[], ALL of them.
nnames counts the PRIMARY pattern's own rows, which are a prefix of the groups[] array.
On a COMPOSED artifact nentries and nnames DIFFER: the rows past nnames are a bound definition's delivered groups ([DD-13b.W1.3]).
Each groups[] row past nnames on a composed artifact carries a non-NULL ref.
rx_info.search_form is a const char * ([OPT-5 STEP 2]): HOW <prefix>_search recovers the match START, mirroring <PREFIX>_DFA_START.
rx_info.search_form "pinned": the start is search_from by compile-time proof, and the artifact carries no reverse machine at all.
rx_info.search_form "reverse-pass": the match start is recovered by a second, backwards scan.
rx_info.search_form is NON-NULL on every artifact that CONTAINS a DFA scan, a VM HYBRID INCLUDED.
rx_info.search_form's guard differs from match_form's (which is "the DFA emitter wrote _match").
rx_info.search_form is NULL only on a plain VM artifact (§6.3).
rx_info.vars is a const char *const * ([VAR]): the variable NAMES the pattern mentions, in first-mention order.
rx_info.vars is NULL when the pattern mentions no variable.
rx_info.nvars is an int: the number of entries in vars[].
rx_info.findings is a const char * ([FINDINGS] B1) mirroring <PREFIX>_FINDINGS: which findings each query this compile asked was answered from (§6.3, findings.md §5).
rx_info.findings is NEVER NULL: it is "" when the compile asked nothing.
rx_info.findings is appended after nvars (the last member): no existing member's offset moved.
rx_info is the canonical machine-readable record (D43), so the <PREFIX>_FINDINGS macro alone would be invisible to a linked binary; hence the findings mirror.
The rx_info.findings value names the analysis a byte-rate came from in plain text, so a shipped binary discloses the analysis name it was built under (findings.md §5; name bundles neutrally).
rx_info.name and rx_info.nentries are appended after match_form: no existing member's offset moved.
rx_info.name answers a different question from <prefix> and is not derivable from it: <prefix> says what the symbols are called; name says what the artifact IS.
A .rxt target <prefix> = <definition> whose definition may carry its own name: one definition built under three configs is three artifacts, three prefixes and ONE name.
rx_info.name lets a consumer walking several <prefix>_info symbols in one binary say these are the same matcher, built differently.
rx_info.name being never NULL is a CONTRACT: a compile that supplies no name stamps its own <prefix>, so a caller needs no NULL branch.
rx_info.name is arbitrary text, not an identifier; nothing derives a symbol from it.
.rxt's own name grammar is stricter than rx_info.name; that is the .rxt format's rule, not this field's.
§6.0's caller algorithm bsearches groups[0 .. nnames).
nnames is the count of the PRIMARY pattern's own named groups, and those rows are a genuine PREFIX of groups[].
nentries is the length of the whole groups[] array.
nnames == nentries on every artifact built from a single pattern, because nothing puts a row in groups[] that the pattern did not declare.
nnames and nentries DIFFER on a composed artifact ([DD-13b.W1.3]).
A caller that wants only the pattern's own names keeps reading nnames; a caller that wants everything in the array reads nentries.
